script.question: When price is ₹20 the quantity demanded is 9 units, and when price is ₹19 the quantity demanded is 10 units. What is the **marginal revenue** from increasing output from **9 units to 10 units**?

lines.say: This question came in the CA Foundation January 2025 exam.
Price is ₹20 and demand is 9 units. Price falls to ₹19 and demand rises to 10 units. Find the marginal revenue of the 10th unit.
MR is the price of the new unit, so it is ₹19. Right?
The right answer is ₹10. Here's why.
Step one. Wrong. MR is the extra total revenue, not the price.
Step two. At 9 units, TR is 9 × 20, which is ₹180.
Step three. At 10 units, TR is 10 × 19, which is ₹190.
Step four. MR is 190 minus 180. That is ₹10.
The shortcut. Price falls on all units. You gain ₹19 on the new unit, but lose ₹1 on each of the 9 old units. 19 minus 9 is 10.
Your turn. Price ₹30 gives 5 units. Price ₹28 gives 6 units. What is the MR of the 6th unit?
